optimizedContext.value:
# Graph Store

## Rules

### Port
- `GraphStore` abstract class (port in domain/ports/, adapters in infrastructure/); `storagePath` constructor param = filesystem root allocated to implementation. Adapters own physical schema, file layout, backend details. Backends MAY differ internally but MUST preserve observable GraphStore API semantics; consumers rely only on abstract semantics.

### Minimum semantics
- Persist FileNode data: canonical workspace-prefixed paths + config-relative file paths + full textual content (content persisted so snippet extraction never re-reads disk at query time); SymbolNode data; SpecNode data; DocumentNode data (textual non-code) incl. upsert/remove operations and full-text document search.
- Persist relation families: IMPORTS, DEFINES, CALLS, CONSTRUCTS, USES_TYPE, EXPORTS, DEPENDS_ON, COVERS_FILE, COVERS_SYMBOL, EXTENDS, IMPLEMENTS, OVERRIDES.
- COVERS_FILE links spec → covered file. COVERS_SYMBOL links spec → covered symbol, MAY carry metadata.stale when archived symbol link no longer resolves live.
- Store-level metadata satisfies statistics/freshness fields: lastIndexedAt, lastIndexedRef, persisted graph fingerprint.
- Incremental indexing matches contentHash before updating node properties or relations.

### Lifecycle + recreation
- open(): Promise<void> prepares backend (module loading, bindings, schema prep, generation checks). close(): Promise<void> idempotent — repeat close or async-dispose combination MUST NOT fail. Ops when unopen/closed throw StoreNotOpenError.
- recreate(): Promise<void> destructive reset stronger than clear(): resets persisted storage layer, not just logical contents. After completion: all indexed data gone, backend ready for fresh indexing run, callers need no knowledge of backend filenames/lockfiles/WAL/schema artifacts. Owning CodeGraphProvider decides recreation within index(...)/clear()/maintenance; host-facing code MUST NOT depend on backend reset mechanics.
- Storage generation marker persisted in graph storage root; destructive recreation rotates it; backend exposes behavior for provider to cache generation at open() and compare before reads (cross-process destructive-replacement detection). Format free (e.g. sidecar graph/storage.epoch).

### Mutations
- upsertFile(file: FileNode, symbols: SymbolNode[], relations: Relation[]): atomic — removes all existing symbols+relations for file path, replaces in single transaction; failure preserves prior state.
- addRelations(relations): purely additive (cross-file relations like CALLS survive file re-upsert).
- removeFile(filePath): atomically removes FileNode, all its SymbolNodes, all Relations where file/symbols are source or target.
- upsertSpec(spec, relations): atomic replace, removes existing DEPENDS_ON where spec is source; removeSpec(specId): removes SpecNode + DEPENDS_ON as source or target.
- Incompatible backend schema MUST reject ordinary reads, never silently recreate empty graph; repair path = destructive full rebuild + storage-generation rotation + full search-index rebuild before readable again. Derived cache state — no incremental migration required.

### Queries
- Single-item: getFile(path), findFilesByConfigRelativePath(path) exact match, getSymbol(id), getSpec(specId), getCallers/getCallees (min CALLS/CONSTRUCTS/USES_TYPE), getImporters/getImportees (IMPORTS), getExtenders/getExtendedTargets (EXTENDS), getImplementors/getImplementedTargets (IMPLEMENTS), getOverriders/getOverriddenTargets (OVERRIDES), getSpecDependencies/getSpecDependents (DEPENDS_ON), getCoveredFiles/getCoveringSpecsForFile (COVERS_FILE), getCoveredSymbols/getCoveringSpecsForSymbol (COVERS_SYMBOL).
- findSymbols(SymbolQuery{ name glob|regex, kinds SymbolKind[], filePath exact|glob, comment substring FTS, caseSensitive default false }).
- Batch traversal: getSymbolsByIds, getIncomingSymbolRelations, getOutgoingSymbolRelations — support CALLS/CONSTRUCTS/USES_TYPE/EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/OVERRIDES. Dedupe inputs without changing meaning; omit unknown ids; deterministic order (symbols by requested id order; relations by source, type, target); empty input → [] with no backend work; no one storage call per symbol/relation type (transparent physical chunking OK).
- Exact batch nodes mirror that contract: getFilesByPaths, getDocumentsByPaths, getSpecsByIds — arbitrary input order, dedupe, preserve first-requested identity order, omit missing, empty → [] no work, no per-identity storage call. Complement single APIs + getAllFiles/getAllDocuments/getAllSpecs (all remain). NOT for display-path derivation (derivable from config alone).
- getStatistics(): GraphStatistics { fileCount, symbolCount, specCount, relationCounts Record<RelationType,number> incl CONSTRUCTS/USES_TYPE/EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/OVERRIDES, languages distinct ids, lastIndexedAt ISO 8601 of last upsertFile, lastIndexedRef VCS ref or null (persisted meta key, read-only via stats), graphFingerprint or null }.
- Bulk: clear() removes all nodes+relations (full re-index); getAllFiles()/getAllSpecs() for incremental diff.

### Search
- searchSymbols/searchSpecs/searchDocuments(SearchOptions) ranked relevance descending; results carry match-aware snippets + 1-based line range startLine..endLine from source content. rebuildFtsIndexes(): maintenance hook after bulk changes where needed.
- Primary identities: specs = canonical specId; symbols = declared name + canonical id; documents = canonical path + alternate identity like configRelativePath if exposed to search. Identity matches rank ahead of body/comment/content-only matches, but candidate retrieval MUST NOT be identity-only; generic text matching (BM25 equivalent) still participates, ranked after identity preference. Backends MAY add identity-derived candidates when tokenizer would miss strong identity hits.
- Lexical token expansion (no user-intent classification): preserve normalized tokens; split whitespace; split separators : / _ . - ; split CamelCase/PascalCase boundaries. core:change → core:change,core,change; ArchiveChange → archivechange,archive,change.
- Identity token-strength order: exact > prefix > suffix > substring. Structured component match (core in core:change) ranks above arbitrary substring (core in score). Higher identity-token coverage improves rank. Examples: specId containing queried capability path outranks content-frequency-only specs; declared name outranks comment-only; path identity outranks body-only.
- SearchOptions: query (required), limit default 20, kind SymbolKind filter (symbols), filePattern glob case-insensitive (symbols), workspace filter, excludePaths globs case-insensitive, excludeWorkspaces names. All filters applied before limit. Score calc + index strategy = implementation concern.

### Reference + coverage persistence
- Atomically persist/retrieve: logical-symbol identity, contributing declarations, symbol spaces, member forms, public/local bindings, binding provenance, per-file/package coverage facts. Distinct bindings/routes between same ordinary relation endpoints stay distinct.
- Selector resolution queries: structured workspace, surface, simple name, symbol space, owner, member form, declaration, public exported name, local scope, coverage status. Rendered canonical ids stay unique external identities; backends MUST NOT parse/case-fold/substring-search serialized id form. Deterministic ordering across backends; no complete graph scan per reference.
- One deterministic complete reference-fact snapshot (incremental hydration retains unaffected facts) + one batched direct-affected-file query over importer/call/construct/type-use/extension/implementation/override relations (affected closure expansion, no per-symbol/per-relation queries).
- Search indexes structured simple name, owner, symbol space, member form, public surface, exported name; groups public bindings under logical target while returning every binding independently and identifying which matched.
- Reverse coverage: batches of canonical file paths + symbol ids → all matching COVERS_FILE/COVERS_SYMBOL relations in deterministic source/type/target order; empty batches → [] no backend work; file-impact traversal covers complete deduplicated blast radius without per-resource calls.

### Source-content candidates
- Persist complete symbol construct + selection ranges; expose backend-neutral source-content candidate query over persisted FileNode.content. Input carries shared normalized complete query, raw terms, expanded terms, category limit, path/workspace filters, exclusions, snippet preference. Output identifies file, backend relevance, enough content/precise occurrence evidence for Code Graph to verify/group exact matches without reading live filesystem.
- Substring-capable content index for ≥3 char queries; defined bounded fallback shorter. MUST NOT scan/return every stored file for ordinary searches. Store yields candidates only — cross-category merging, provenance, symbol-aware suppression, final ranking, grouping, post-suppression limits belong to Code Graph application use case.

### Freshness persistence
- Persist backend-neutral IndexedInputObservation records separate from semantic nodes: workspace, logical resource kind + id, filesystem/repository input kind, non-absolute logical locator, indexed content hash, optional observed mtime/size or repository revision, monotonic stale flag.
- Files/documents normally map to one observation; aggregate specs map to every content-artifact/metadata/persisted-state input producing the node.
- Batch reads + compare-and-set mutations support marking stale, refreshing equal-content observations, atomically marking affected workspace + global latches; assessment started before reindexing must not mutate new evidence.
- One monotonic knownStaleSinceLastIndex latch per workspace + one aggregate latch. Only successful indexing clears stale input/latch state; transient unknown assessments NEVER persisted as stale.

### Bulk indexing session
- Backend-neutral session: begin once, accept bounded file/document/spec/symbol/semantic-fact/observation/relation chunks, commit once, rebuild semantic + source-content search indexes once post-commit. Relation endpoint validation + hierarchy/method lookup via batch ops; no existence/hierarchy Store call per relation. Dedupe equivalent relations across chunks. Failed session MUST NOT expose partially committed generation.

## Constraints

- Abstract class, not interface (project port convention)
- All mutations atomic at file level — no partial updates
- Backend-agnostic contract: no prescribed backend, physical schema, or filesystem layout
- Destructive reset modeled through recreate() owned by provider/indexing flows, never caller-managed backend file deletion
- Generation markers exist for provider-owned cross-process stale detection
- No dependency on @specd/core — error types extend CodeGraphError
